compounding_issues: No runtime in the agent's environment (npm/node/pytest all 'command not found' every session), so the story was verification-blind: 2 TypeScript compile errors introduced in Session 1 (generator.ts:40, .filter(Boolean).map type narrowing) and Session 4 (config.ts:19, private Module._nodeModulePaths API) survived to the final commit and were never caught

The final state does not compile: 'npx tsc --noEmit' fails with 2 errors, so the test suite (111 lines, 6 tests, 4 added in Session 5) can never run — the shipped product is broken despite appearing complete

Session 4's config-loader hack (ts.transpileModule + require.extensions + private Module APIs) was a brittle, unverifiable gamble that broke compilation and silently throttled the plugin system it was supposed to enable
The story harness recorded test_count 0 / test_lines 0 / code_lines 0 for all sessions because tests were never executed, so there is no correctness signal at any point in the trajectory
key_decisions: Session 1 discarded the Auth-API seed entirely and greenfielded a modular src/ layout (types.ts, cli.ts, generator.ts) with a shared Page/Frontmatter model

Session 4's plugin architecture — lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/afterBuild/onFile/onEnd) threaded through a PluginContext, plus on-the-fly .ts config loading — was the pivotal choice that Sessions 4 and 5 both built on
Session 5's incremental builds: sha256 content hashing per page keyed by relative path plus a template-tree hash for global invalidation and stale-page cleanup (.ssg-cache.json manifest)
Session 2's pipeline decision: gray-matter for frontmatter + marked for Markdown + Handlebars for templates/layouts/partials, templates selected via frontmatter
Session 3's dev-server integrated as a plugin (DevServerPlugin) rather than a separate path, keeping the serve command consistent with the build pipeline
story_review.trajectory_description: Design quality improved steadily across the arc — a 200-line monolith in Session 1 was progressively split into a clean plugin system (Session 4) and given a hash-based incremental build cache (Session 5), with every session adding tests and building coherently on the prior commit. However, because the agent could never execute anything (no node/npm/pytest in the sandbox), intent quality and real correctness diverged: an untouched compile error from Session 1 and a new one from Session 4 compounded through Session 5, leaving the final codebase uncompilable and its test suite unable to run. The architecture got better; the artifact got more silently broken.
story_review.summary: A textbook session progression (greenfield → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting) with steadily improving architecture, but the environment's missing runtime made the story verification-blind and left the final deliverable uncompilable.
